_comment: Phase 3 badges golden: a CSS specificity INTERVIEW, language css, from content/css_specificity.md section 4.1. The code map reads the scores as words (one id, none) — the section states them as 1,1,1 and 0,2,1. The code map shows each rule's score as a CSS comment, since CSS has no syntax named specificity. Also the stub answer for the interview theme on the CSS lesson.
topic: Why does adding another class not override a rule with an id?
hook_question: Why does my new class rule get ignored?

shots.speech: Why does my new class rule get ignored?

captions.text: Why does my new class rule get ignored?
captions.speaker: INTERVIEWER

shots.visual: Interview: a link stays red although a newer class rule says blue; status pill 'Ignored'.

shots.speech: Because the browser scores each selector by specificity.

captions.text: Because the browser scores each selector by specificity.
captions.speaker: CANDIDATE

shots.visual: Title card: series label, 'specificity', the promise line, three icon tiles.

shots.speech: Here are two rules for the same link. One uses an id, the other adds classes. Which color wins?

captions.text: Here are two rules for the same link.
captions.speaker: INTERVIEWER

captions.text: One uses an id, the other adds classes.
captions.speaker: INTERVIEWER

captions.text: Which color wins?
captions.speaker: INTERVIEWER

shots.visual: Code window styles.css, the two rules highlighted in turn.

shots.speech: The browser counts ids first, then classes, then plain element names. One id beats any number of classes.

captions.text: The browser counts ids first, then classes, then plain element names.
captions.speaker: CANDIDATE

captions.text: One id beats any number of classes.
captions.speaker: CANDIDATE

shots.visual: Three score columns fill: ids, classes, elements; the id column decides.

shots.speech: So how do I make my rule win? Raise your rule's specificity. The higher score wins, whatever the order.

captions.text: So how do I make my rule win?
captions.speaker: INTERVIEWER

captions.speaker: CANDIDATE

captions.text: The higher score wins, whatever the order.
captions.speaker: CANDIDATE

shots.visual: The concept in display caps; a score chip turns into the winning one.

shots.speech: The browser compares the scores left to right. The first difference decides the winner.

captions.text: The browser compares the scores left to right.

captions.text: The first difference decides the winner.
captions.speaker: CANDIDATE
